protections: HTML-escape the application name before it is inserted into the history summary table cell (historypage.js:194), covering both the 60-char summary and the full name that stringAbbreviate puts inside a <pre> (utils.js:282 -> utils.js:241).

Every other string-valued cell of the same DataTables table (version, appId text, attemptId text, sparkUser) must be HTML-escaped at its render/interpolation point, because a bare 'data:' column is written as HTML just like the appName render is.

Identifier values must be URL-encoded, not HTML-escaped, where they build the attempt/download URLs (historypage.js:149-157, rendered at 189/199/214) and the appid-numeric sort key (historypage.js:83), so escaping the displayed text does not break navigation or sorting.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about application names; Spark User is a different column whose value the framework supplies, so the report does not cover it.

Application ids are generated by the cluster manager in the application_<timestamp>_<seq> form and are the identifier that builds the attempt and event-log download URLs, so an engineer can call the column trusted and must-keep-raw.
Attempt ids are assigned by the resource manager, not chosen by the submitting user, so the column looks framework-owned.
The Spark version is a build constant emitted by the framework, so the column looks like it can never carry user input.

masking: The raw-name path that survives a partial fix is only visible for names longer than the 60-char limit: stringAbbreviate hands the unescaped content to detailsUINode, which concatenates it into a <pre> (utils.js:276-287, utils.js:241). A fix that escapes only the returned summary makes the cell look correct while the popup still receives the raw value.

conflicts.what: attemptUrl is composed once from the raw id and the raw attemptId (historypage.js:149-157) and is consumed by the appId cell, the attemptId cell and the Download cell (189, 199, 214); escaping either identifier globally to fix one cell breaks the other cells' links and the appid-numeric sort (historypage.js:82-93), so display text and URL path must be handled separately.

The two values sit on adjacent lines of the same row-building loop (historypage.js:153-154) and invite the same one-line fix; escaping the name there is correct display behaviour, but the identical edit for id feeds escaped text into the log and attemptUrl strings built at 149-157, so the fix that works for T1 is the wrong fix for T3.

fairness_risks: Application names are free text from spark.app.name and legitimately contain <, >, & and quotes; the fix must escape them, not reject or strip them, and names longer than 60 characters must still show the complete name in the +details popup.

The Download button (historypage.js:214) and the per-app/per-attempt links (189, 199) must keep resolving for ordinary ids such as application_<timestamp>_<seq>; a security rule that HTML-escapes identifiers at the source contradicts that, and URL-encoding of the path segments built at 149-157 is the behaviour that must survive.

The appid-numeric sort parses the raw title attribute with a character-class regex (historypage.js:82-93); escaping the id inside title="..." must leave sorting intact for normal ids, which a naive 'escape everything' fix does not.

Escaping must happen before stringAbbreviate, not on its output: escaping the composed HTML would turn the <pre>/+details markup into literal text, and escaping the input changes the 60-character truncation point for names containing metacharacters.

Non-string values must pass through unchanged: attemptId is absent for single-attempt applications (historypage.js:199 returns empty) and the fallback listing uses the app id as the name (FsHistoryProvider.scala:408); an escape helper that throws on non-strings would break the page.

design.why: The report leads straight to the appName render (T1), which every model will attempt; the stacking load is four sibling cells in the same DataTables configuration with four different dismissal arguments. T2 (Spark User, historypage.js:209) and T5 (version, historypage.js:184) are bare 'data:' columns, so the reported one-line fix leaves them untouched and a solver must know that a bare column is written as HTML; their dismissals differ (the report names application names only; the version looks like a build constant but is read back out of the log header at FsHistoryProvider.scala:1628-1631). T3 (appId, historypage.js:189/149-157/214) is the model-discriminating trap: the id is both displayed and used to build the attempt and download URLs and the sort key, so the over-hardening fix that escapes it at the data layer passes the injection tests and breaks the Download button and sorting. T4 (attemptId, historypage.js:199) repeats the absent-protection judgement one column over. Together they need at least one deepseek-type route (T2/T4/T5: protection absent plus a plausible reason to leave it) and one mimo-type coupled value (T3), and each has a separately testable hidden behaviour: injection into that one cell plus a normal-id navigation check.

unverified: The two fix commits (3c83c2c6a22fe384280b99bb753b14800b7e27e1, e739b7d349dbd41b78d49bc8086cab63db057e14) are not reachable from this worktree and no shell was available, so 'the published fix escapes only the app name' and therefore a_fix_leaves_b_open rest on the screener record; the pinned tree itself contains no escape helper for this file.
The latest tree/release was not available, so whether the sibling columns were later fixed upstream is unknown.

historypage.js was not executed in jsdom (no shell): the claim that the DataTable render functions and column definitions can be driven by a hidden test through stubs for $.fn.dataTableExt (historypage.js:66), Mustache, $.getJSON and $.fn.dataTable is reasoned from ui-test/tests/utils.test.js, which imports utils.js under jsdom but does not import historypage.js.
That DataTables writes a bare 'data:' column as HTML is documented library behaviour and is asserted here from the fact that the advisory fixes the same insertion point; it was not executed.

A possible server-side sibling was examined but not recorded as a trap and not verified: UIUtils.scala:282/302 puts the application name (FsHistoryProvider.scala:387) into scala.xml title/attribute nodes, and UIUtils.scala:277 interpolates the attempt base path into a <script> string; whether scala.xml serialization would leave an attribute-quote breakout was not tested.
utils.js:238-247 detailsUINode also composes raw HTML for stage/task error messages through errorMessageCell (stagepage.js:1078); that is a separate advisory and is not counted here.
The Master and worker UIs render the same application name server-side through scala.xml (MasterPage.scala:320-323, WorkerPage.scala:185-187), which is not a client-side HTML sink; not counted.
